#### Thinking

Two issues in the minimap:

1. `_update_minimap` generates a new ImageTexture every time it updates (GPU texture allocation per movement). Minor but real issue: can reuse by updating `_map_image` and calling `_map_rect.texture.update(_map_image)` on the existing ImageTexture. Saves about 20 textures per minute during walking. Cheap improvement, low risk.

2. MAP_GRID 60 → 3600 height_at calls per update (analytical, at current speeds about 0.19ms per call... 25921 calls in 811ms = 31µs/call → 3600×31µs ≈ 113ms hitch on every update!). This is a noticeable stutter during walking (every 6m of movement = 113ms freeze). This is a runtime hitch! Options:
   - Reduce MAP_GRID to 40 (1600 calls ≈ 50ms) — still a hitch.
   - Spread updates across frames (progressive: sample N cells per frame) — better.
   - Use a cached coarse grid: sample from a precomputed analytical height grid? Trees/rocks also use height_at, but the big cost is minimap updates during movement.
   - Bilinear sample from the collision hgrid (3.9m cells, radius 90 → 45 cell span → 22×22 grid samples from a 3.9m cache = blurry, but since the minimap is for height overview display, no problem!). Even better: cache the entire analytical grid at higher resolution just for minimap lookups? The minimap displays a large-scale height overview — bilinear on a 3.9m grid is visually enough (each minimap cell = 180/60 = 3m on the ground).

   Simplest and most robust: store hgrid in terrain during collision construction, add height_at_cached(x,z) with bilinear; HUD uses it (falls back to analytical if not ready). ~O(1) per sample → minimap updates become about 1ms. And no hitches.

   Even simpler: progressive sampling with chunked updates. The bilinear cache is cleaner.

Implementation in terrain.gd: store hgrid and parameters in _build_collision_faces; add function:

```gdscript
var _grid: PackedFloat32Array
var _grid_n := 0
var _grid_half := 0.0
var _grid_cell := 1.0

func height_at_fast(x: float, z: float) -> float:
    if _grid.is_empty():
        return _height_at(x, z)
    var fx := (x + _grid_half) / _grid_cell
    var fz := (z + _grid_half) / _grid_cell
    ... clamp, bilinear
```

Bilinear of the fbm field at 3.9m cells: smooth small bumps at n3's 6x frequency: wavelength? fbm octave at freq*6 ≈ 0.054 cycles/m → period 18.5m, plus the small high-freq detail in vnoise has 1-unit period in noise space... The base lattice of fbm is p=pos*frequency → lattice spacing 111m; subsequent octaves: 4x → 27.8m, 6x → 18.5m, plus rotations double it each time: up to about 1.7m-period octaves (last octave 0.009×6×2^4=0.864? no wait, fbm has 5 octaves doubling 2.02 each time → final octave frequency ≈ base×16×6×0.009 ≈ 0.86 cycles/m → 1.16m period!). Bilinear at 3.9m can't capture 1.2m ripples — minimap colors will smooth out. Fine for minimap purposes (altitude overview), visually within acceptable range. But if trees/rocks use fast lookup, the alignment with visuals breaks (sinking/floating rocks). So: minimap only.

Also fix texture reuse. And remove the map's "delta" parameter? _process(delta) no longer uses delta — signature is fine (unused parameter warning? _process(delta: float) — if named delta, no warning).

Wait, is the minimap really causing hitches? 113ms every 6m of movement at walk speed (about 5m/s) → every ~1.2s. Yeah, definitely noticeable. Fix it.

Also, `_map_image.resize` after set_pixel — resize operates on CPU image, then creates texture. Fine.

```json
	var shape := ConcavePolygonShape3D.new()
	shape.set_faces(_build_collision_faces())
	var body := StaticBody3D.new()
	var csc := CollisionShape3D.new()
	csc.shape = shape
	body.add_child(csc)
	add_child(body)
```

Design:
- Node3D Sword (child of Camera3D). Pivot for the pose; a MeshInstance3D "Blade" child holds the geometry built from boxes/cylinders.
- Rest pose (sword held low-right, blade pointing up-forward): position (0.38, -0.32, -0.55), rotation roughly (-20° X tilt, 15° Y).
- Slash: a diagonal downward swing from upper-right to lower-left (classic):
  - windup: raise up-right and rotate back (0.14s, ease-out)
  - slash: whip across to lower-left with a wrist roll (0.16s, ease-in) — emit "slashed" at the midpoint for hit detection
  - recovery: return to rest pose (0.3s, ease-in-out)
- Idle sway: sin-based micro-offsets; movement sway: read the player's velocity? Keep it simple: time-based sway only, plus a slight lag from camera rotation? Skip the lag.
- Sword meshes:
  - Blade: BoxMesh (0.045, 0.012, 0.62), metallic steel (roughness 0.25, metallic 0.9), positioned so it extends in the -Z direction: center z=-0.35.
  - Tip: small rotated box? Use a scaled BoxMesh rotated 45° for the tip, or a cylinder. Keep it: blade + a thin "edge highlight" box (emissive?) nah, skip.
  - Guard: Box (0.16, 0.03, 0.03), z=-0.04.
  - Grip: CylinderMesh (r=0.018, h=0.16) rotated 90° on X axis, z=+0.06, dark brown.
  - Pommel: SphereMesh r=0.025, z=+0.15.
- Orientation: build the sword along the -Z direction (forward). The rest pose tilts the blade slightly upward.
- cast_shadow off (view models typically don't cast into the world; but the shadow pass will draw it anyway; set OFF to save perf).
- Layers: could put on a separate layer to avoid clipping into walls — skip (camera near 0.05 default; sword is at 0.55m so it's fine).

Z input: inside sword.gd's _unhandled_input: `if event is InputEventKey and event.pressed and not event.echo and event.keycode == KEY_Z: attack()`. But player.gd's _unhandled_input handles mouse capture etc.; Z is unused elsewhere. Note: when mouse is released (ESC menu) — should attack still work? Either way is fine.

Tween: create_tween(); chain with tween_property + tween_callback. Use TRANS_CUBIC/QUART etc. Animate the pivot's `position` and `rotation_degrees` (Node3D rotation is Euler angles — Tweening Euler angles is fine for small ranges; slash is a big rotation — Euler interpolation might look weird but acceptable for a stylized swing. Alternative: Tween the quaternion via a custom method: tween_method with spherical interpolation — better: tween_method with _apply_pose(t, pose) that lerps position and Basis slerp. Keep Euler Tween, tune angles to stay within ±180.

Poses (position, rotation_degrees):
- REST: pos (0.38, -0.30, -0.50), rot (-15, 20, -10)  [X tilt raises the tip? Blade is along -Z; rotating -15 on X pitches the tip up]
- WINDUP: pos (0.50, -0.10, -0.62), rot (-55, 45, -35) — raise up-back-right, tilt the wrist
- SLASH_END: pos (0.10, -0.45, -0.70), rot (25, -35, 30) — swing across to lower-left, follow-through
- Recovery → REST.

Emit `slash_hit` signal at about 60% of the slash. Also small camera feedback: skip (player handles movement; avoid coupling).

#### Thinking

User request: The blade performs a large circular/rotational swing, while the grip (handle) only follows with small adjustments — that is, the pivot of the rotation is placed near the hand/handle, and the blade traces out a big circle. A flowing sword-swinging motion, natural, combat stance, motion blur, realistic action. The blade's rotation amplitude must be clearly larger than the handle's.

Interpretation: Currently the entire sword (handle + blade) is being rotated as a rigid body. What they want is a "whirl (circular swing)" where the blade sweeps a big arc around the hand — physically, when you swing a sword, the hand rotates around the wrist/grip, and the tip of the blade traces a large circle. To make the blade's rotation amplitude far exceed the handle's:

Implementation approach: Add a hierarchy:
- Sword (root, camera-local) = hand position: only small movements/rotations (position drift + slight rotation ±10-15°).
- Child node "BladePivot" placed at the grip end (near the hand) — the blade geometry is offset from this pivot; this pivot performs large-amplitude rotation (full 360° circular / multi-turn winding).

So the animation: during the attack, the BladePivot rotates 360°+ (or more) around an axis (e.g., a Z or X axis through the hand, plus yaw), while the root only moves slightly and rotates slightly. The blade mesh must be attached to the pivot at a distance from the rotation center (the blade extends outward from the grip), so that the tip traces a huge circle, while the grip (attached to the root) only rotates slightly.

Restructuring the sword.gd scene tree:
- Sword (Node3D, root, camera-local) — "hand/grip" node: holds the grip, guard, pommel meshes (the handle assembly), positioned near the hand.
- BladePivot (Node3D child of root, placed at the grip end / where the fingers hold, i.e., the z just in front of the guard): holds the blade + fuller + tip meshes, extending in the -Z direction from the pivot. The pivot does large-amplitude circular rotation.

Wait — physically the blade is rigidly attached to the guard; if the blade rotates around the wrist and the guard stays still, the joint between the guard and blade will visibly break. But the user explicitly wants "clearly distinguish the motion of the blade and the handle, with the blade's rotation amplitude far larger than the handle's" — the blade's rotation is far larger than the handle's. So the guard/handle follows with small rotation, and the blade whirls around. To avoid visual disconnection, place the pivot at the base of the blade (just in front of the guard): the blade rotates around its own base — like a fan rotating around its axis. The handle only sways slightly. The joint stays connected (the blade's base is at the pivot center, and the handle end stays near the guard). This is a stylized "blade whirl" effect.

```bash
import numpy as np

])

f = np.array([0.30, 0.35, -0.886]); f /= np.linalg.norm(f)   # 刃向
Zs = -f
Ys = np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0])
Xs = np.cross(Ys, Zs); Xs /= np.linalg.norm(Xs)
Ys = np.cross(Zs, Xs); Ys /= np.linalg.norm(Ys)
S = np.column_stack([Xs, Ys, Zs])
R = H.T @ S   # 正交，逆=转置
print("R rows:")
for row in R: print("  Vector3(%.3f, %.3f, %.3f)," % tuple(row))
# 欧拉角(与 Godot from_euler YXZ? 默认XYZ顺序) 打印矩阵即可
EOF
```

The user wants the swing animation to be more exaggerated. Currently the sword follows the mocap's wrist trajectory 1:1. To exaggerate: amplify the deviation of the hand's motion from the rest pose.

Implementation in sword.gd's _process:
- Record a reference pose: capture the wrist's local transform (relative to the rig) at idle start (first frame of Idle_Sword, or average). Since idle sways slightly, use a fixed reference captured once after the rig loads (e.g., rig's transform * bone's global pose at frame 0).
- Compute delta = ref.inverse() * current (local-space delta of hand movement).
- Amplify: delta_pos *= POS_GAIN (e.g., 2.2), delta_rot: convert to axis-angle, angle *= ROT_GAIN (e.g., 1.8).
- final = ref * amplified_delta, then transform to camera space (ref is captured in camera space, since rig is a child of camera → constant).

Rotation amplification: extract angle from Basis: use Basis.get_axis_and_angle()? Godot 4: does Basis.get_angle() exist? There's `Basis.get_axis_angle()`, hmm — actually Godot 4 has `Basis.get_euler()`, and also `Basis.get_axis_and_angle(axis, angle)`? No — Godot 4 removed get_axis_and_angle (3.x had it; 4.x: `Basis.get_rotation_quaternion()`, then Quaternion.angle() and Axis — yes, Quaternion has angle and axis properties). So: q = delta.basis.get_rotation_quaternion(); ang = q.angle(); ax = q.axis(); amplified = Quaternion(ax, ang * gain).

Position: delta.origin * gain.

Note: The reference pose must be captured in a stable coordinate system. The rig is a child of the camera, and the camera rotates with the viewpoint. The wrist's global transform rotates with the camera. The delta between the current global value and the reference global value only works if the camera's orientation is the same. Solution: capture the reference in the rig's local space: ref_local = rig.global.affine_inverse() * hand.global (captured once). Per frame: cur_local = rig.global.affine_inverse() * hand.global; delta = ref_local.inverse() * cur_local; amp; final_local = ref_local * amp; sword.global = rig.global * final_local * HAND_CORRECTION. Since rig is a child of camera, it moves with the viewpoint.

- Gains as exported-style constants: ROT_GAIN 1.7, POS_GAIN 2.2.
- _process: compute as above.

Quaternion amplification: angle near zero → axis is NaN; guard: only if ang > 1e-4.

Compute the affine for each parallelogram:
def paste_parallelogram(canvas, img, origin, u, v):
  w,h = img.size; scale u to the full span: u is the vector for the width, v for the height.
  Output region bbox: corners o, o+u, o+v, o+u+v.
  For each pixel (X,Y) in the bbox: solve (s,t) such that (X,Y)=o + s*u + v*t (s is [0,1]) → s,t = inv([[ux,vx],[uy,vy]]) · (X-ox, Y-oy). Then source pixel = (s*w, t*h).
  PIL's AFFINE transform coefficients map output→input directly: input = (a*X+b*Y+c, d*X+e*Y+f) (global canvas coordinates). So a..f from the inverse matrix: [s*w] = M_inv * ([X,Y]-o) * w… compute M=[[ux,vy],[uy,vx]]? Note: p = o + s*u + t*v → [X-ox, Y-oy] = [[ux,vx],[uy,vy]]·[s,t]. inv = 1/det * [[vy,-vx],[-uy,ux]], det=ux*vy-vx*uy. s = (vy*(X-ox) - vx*(Y-oy))/det; t = (-uy*(X-ox)+ux*(Y-oy))/det. Input pixel = (s*w, t*h). So a=vy*w/det, b=-vx*w/det, c= -(vy*ox - vx*oy)*w/det, d=-uy*h/det, e=ux*h/det, f=(uy*ox-ux*oy)*h/det.
  Crop the bbox region from the canvas with transform(bbox_size, AFFINE, (a',b',c',d',e',f')) with offsets.

```bash
python - <<'EOF'
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
import os
d = r"C:/Users/xiaomi.h/.qwenworkcn/workspace/mt9ivdjpdp3ogfvg/dl/dogmilk"
front = Image.open(os.path.join(d,"panel_b.png")).convert("RGB")
back  = Image.open(os.path.join(d,"panel_a.png")).convert("RGB")

W,H = 900, 900
canvas = Image.new("RGB",(W,H),(245,247,250))

def paste_para(img, o, u, v):
    w,h = img.size
    ux,uy = u; vx,vy = v
    det = ux*vy - vx*uy
    corners = [o, (o[0]+ux,o[1]+uy), (o[0]+vx,o[1]+vy), (o[0]+ux+vx,o[1]+uy+vy)]
    xs=[c[0] for c in corners]; ys=[c[1] for c in corners]
    x0,y0,x1,y1 = int(min(xs)),int(min(ys)),int(max(xs)),int(max(ys))
    a = vy*w/det; b = -vx*w/det; c0 = -(vy*o[0]-vx*o[1])*w/det
    dd = -uy*h/det; e = ux*h/det; f = (uy*o[0]-ux*o[1])*h/det
    region = img.transform((x1-x0, y1-y0), Image.AFFINE,
        (a, b, c0 - (a*x0+b*y0), dd, e, f - (dd*x0+e*y0)))
    mask = Image.new("L",(x1-x0,y1-y0),0)
    from PIL import ImageDraw as D2
    mp = [(cx-x0,cy-y0) for cx,cy in corners]
    D2.Draw(mask).polygon(mp, fill=255)
    canvas.paste(region,(x0,y0),mask)

# 正面：略梯形（透视感弱化为矩形）
paste_para(front.resize((380,560)), (180,270), (380,0), (0,560))
# 右侧面：向后上方斜
paste_para(back.resize((150,560)), (560,270), (150,-55), (0,560))
# 顶面：蓝色封盖
top = Image.new("RGB",(380,150),(38,90,168))
dr = ImageDraw.Draw(top)
dr.rectangle([0,60,380,90], fill=(250,250,250))
paste_para(top, (180,270), (380,0), (150,-55))
# 底部阴影
sh = ImageDraw.Draw(canvas)
sh.polygon([(170,835),(570,835),(725,775),(320,775)], fill=(215,220,228))
canvas.paste(canvas)  # noop keep
canvas.save(os.path.join(d,"mockup.png"))
print("saved", os.path.join(d,"mockup.png"))
EOF
```

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
import os
d = r"C:/Users/xiaomi.h/.qwenworkcn/workspace/mt9ivdjpdp3ogfvg/dl/dogmilk"
front = Image.open(os.path.join(d,"panel_b.png")).convert("RGB")
back  = Image.open(os.path.join(d,"panel_a.png")).convert("RGB")
```bash
W,H = 900,900
canvas = Image.new("RGB",(W,H),(245,247,250))

def paste_para(img, o, u, v):
    w,h = img.size
    ux,uy = u; vx,vy = v
    det = ux*vy - vx*uy
    corners = [o,(o[0]+ux,o[1]+uy),(o[0]+vx,o[1]+vy),(o[0]+ux+vx,o[1]+uy+vy)]
    xs=[c[0] for c in corners]; ys=[c[1] for c in corners]
    x0,y0,x1,y1 = int(min(xs)),int(min(ys)),int(max(xs)),int(max(ys))
    a = vy*w/det; b = -vx*w/det; c = -(vy*o[0]-vx*o[1])*w/det
    dd = -uy*h/det; e = ux*h/det; f = (uy*o[0]-ux*o[1])*h/det
    region = img.transform((x1-x0,y1-y0), Image.AFFINE,
        (a, b, c + a*x0 + b*y0, dd, e, f + dd*x0 + e*y0))
    mask = Image.new("L",(x1-x0,y1-y0),0)
    ImageDraw.Draw(mask).polygon([(cx-x0,cy-y0) for cx,cy in corners], fill=255)
    canvas.paste(region,(x0,y0),mask)

paste_para(front.resize((380,560)), (180,270), (380,0), (0,560))
paste_para(back.resize((150,560)), (560,270), (150,-55), (0,560))
top = Image.new("RGB",(380,150),(38,90,168))
ImageDraw.Draw(top).rectangle([0,60,380,90], fill=(250,250,250))
paste_para(top, (180,270), (380,0), (150,-55))
ImageDraw.Draw(canvas).polygon([(170,835),(570,835),(725,775),(320,775)], fill=(215,220,228))
canvas.save(os.path.join(d,"mockup.png"))
print("ok")
EOF
```

#### Tool: Bash

```bash
python - <<'EOF'
import os, numpy as np, trimesh
from PIL import Image
d = r"C:/Users/xiaomi.h/.qwenworkcn/workspace/mt9ivdjpdp3ogfvg/dl/dogmilk"
front = Image.open(os.path.join(d,"panel_b.png")).convert("RGB")
back  = Image.open(os.path.join(d,"panel_a.png")).convert("RGB")
side  = front.resize((160,558))  # 侧面用正面图案压缩
top   = Image.new("RGB",(300,160),(38,90,168))
from PIL import ImageDraw
ImageDraw.Draw(top).rectangle([0,60,300,100], fill=(245,245,245))
bot   = Image.new("RGB",(300,160),(120,130,140))

# 盒子尺寸（米）：宽0.09 x 高0.25 x 厚0.06
W,H,D = 0.09,0.25,0.06
def face(img, verts):
    m = trimesh.Trimesh(vertices=np.array(verts,dtype=np.float64), faces=[[0,1,2],[0,2,3]], process=False)
    m.visual = trimesh.visual.TextureVisuals(uv=np.array([[0,0],[1,0],[1,1],[0,1]]), image=img)
    return m
hx,hy,hz = W/2,H/2,D/2
cy = H/2
faces = {
 "front": face(front, [(-hx,0,hz),(hx,0,hz),(hx,H,hz),(-hx,H,hz)]),
 "back":  face(back,  [(hx,0,-hz),(-hx,0,-hz),(-hx,H,-hz),(hx,H,-hz)]),
 "right": face(side,  [(hx,0,hz),(hx,0,-hz),(hx,H,-hz),(hx,H,hz)]),
 "left":  face(side,  [(-hx,0,-hz),(-hx,0,hz),(-hx,H,hz),(-hx,H,-hz)]),
 "top":   face(top,   [(-hx,H,hz),(hx,H,hz),(hx,H,-hz),(-hx,H,-hz)]),
 "bottom":face(bot,   [(-hx,0,-hz),(hx,0,-hz),(hx,0,hz),(-hx,0,hz)]),
}
scene = trimesh.Scene(faces)
out = r"E:/游戏大乱斗/assets/props"
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
p = os.path.join(out,"wild_dog_milk.glb")
scene.export(p)
print("saved", p, os.path.getsize(p)//1024, "KB")
EOF
```

Two fixes:
1. player.gd: PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.create(from, to, [get_rid()]) — the signature is create(origin, destination, collision_mask: int = 4294967295, hit_from_inside: bool = false). The 3rd argument is a mask, not an exclude array. Use create(from,to), and then set .exclude afterward:
```
var q := PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.create(from, to)
q.exclude = [get_rid()]
var hit := ...intersect_ray(q)
```
2. boss.gd: ProgressBar3D doesn't exist in Godot 4.7?? Actually, ProgressBar3D should have been added in Godot 4.0... hmm, "Could not find type ProgressBar3D" — maybe it's only available when the UI module is included... no, it exists in standard Godot 4 (ProgressBar3D inherits from Range3D). import os, numpy as np, trimesh
```bash
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
d = r"C:/Users/xiaomi.h/.qwenworkcn/workspace/mt9ivdjpdp3ogfvg/dl/dogmilk"
front = Image.open(os.path.join(d,"panel_b.png")).convert("RGB")
back  = Image.open(os.path.join(d,"panel_a.png")).convert("RGB")
# 侧面：用正面图案横向压缩（保证明亮），背板用 panel_a
side  = front.resize((150, 558))
top   = Image.new("RGB",(300,160),(38,90,168))
ImageDraw.Draw(top).rectangle([0,60,300,100], fill=(245,245,245))
bot   = Image.new("RGB",(300,160),(150,160,170))

W,H,D = 0.09,0.25,0.06
hx,hy,hz = W/2, H/2, D/2
uv = np.array([[0,0],[1,0],[1,1],[0,1]], dtype=np.float64)

def face(img, verts, normal):
    v = np.array(verts, dtype=np.float64)
    m = trimesh.Trimesh(vertices=v, faces=[[0,1,2],[0,2,3]], process=False)
    n = np.array([normal]*4, dtype=np.float64)
    m.vertex_normals = n
    m.visual = trimesh.visual.TextureVisuals(uv=uv, image=img)
    return m

# 顶点顺序全部按"从外侧看逆时针"，法线显式指定，杜绝黑面
faces = {
 "front":  face(front, [(-hx,0,hz),(hx,0,hz),(hx,H,hz),(-hx,H,hz)], (0,0,1)),
 "back":   face(back,  [(hx,0,-hz),(-hx,0,-hz),(-hx,H,-hz),(hx,H,-hz)], (0,0,-1)),
 "right":  face(side,  [(hx,0,hz),(hx,0,-hz),(hx,H,-hz),(hx,H,hz)], (1,0,0)),
 "left":   face(side,  [(-hx,0,-hz),(-hx,0,hz),(-hx,H,hz),(-hx,H,-hz)], (-1,0,0)),
 "top":    face(top,   [(-hx,H,hz),(hx,H,hz),(hx,H,-hz),(-hx,H,-hz)], (0,1,0)),
 "bottom": face(bot,   [(-hx,0,-hz),(hx,0,-hz),(hx,0,hz),(-hx,0,hz)], (0,-1,0)),
}
scene = trimesh.Scene(faces)
p = r"E:/游戏大乱斗/assets/props/wild_dog_milk.glb"
scene.export(p)
print("rebuilt", os.path.getsize(p)//1024, "KB")
EOF
```

```json
		["side.png", Vector3(1, 0, 0), [Vector3(hx, 0, hz), Vector3(hx, 0, -hz), Vector3(hx, H, -hz), Vector3(hx, H, hz)]],

	]
	var uvs := PackedVector2Array([Vector2(0, 1), Vector2(1, 1), Vector2(1, 0), Vector2(0, 0)])
	var mesh := ArrayMesh.new()
	for def in defs:
		var st := SurfaceTool.new()

		mesh.surface_set_material(mesh.get_surface_count() - 1, _face_mat(def[0]))
```

```json
61				var h: float = ground.height_at(x, z)
62				if h > best_h:
63					best_h = h
64					best = Vector3(x, h + 2.0, z)
65		return best
66	
67	
68	func take_damage(amount: int) -> void:
69		## 受到伤害：扣血并发出 hp_changed，血量归零时发出 died
70		if amount <= 0:
71			return
72		hp = clampi(hp - amount, 0, max_hp)
73		hp_changed.emit(hp, max_hp)
74		if hp == 0:
75			died.emit()
76	
77	
78	func heal(amount: int) -> void:
79		## 治疗：回血并发出 hp_changed
80		if amount <= 0 or hp >= max_hp:
81			return
82		hp = clampi(hp + amount, 0, max_hp)
83		hp_changed.emit(hp, max_hp)
84	
85	
86	func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
87		if event is InputEventMouseMotion and Input.mouse_mode == Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED:
88			# 水平：绕 Y 轴旋转身体；垂直：仅旋转相机并限制角度
89			rotate_y(-event.relative.x * mouse_sensitivity)
90			$Camera3D.rotate_x(-event.relative.y * mouse_sensitivity)
91			$Camera3D.rotation.x = clampf($Camera3D.rotation.x, -1.5, 1.5)
92		elif event is InputEventMouseButton:
93			if event.pressed and event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT:
94				Input.mouse_mode = Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED
95		elif event is InputEventKey and event.pressed and not event.echo:
96			if event.is_action_pressed("ui_cancel"):
97				# ESC：在捕获与释放之间切换
98				if Input.mouse_mode == Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED:
99					Input.mouse_mode = Input.MOUSE_MODE_VISIBLE
100				else:
101					Input.mouse_mode = Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED
102			elif event.keycode == KEY_F:
103				# 调试键：F 受伤 10 点（验证血条用，之后可删）
104				take_damage(10)
105			elif event.keycode == KEY_G:
106				# 调试键：G 治疗 10 点（验证血条用，之后可删）
107				heal(10)
108	
109	
110	func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
111		# 掉出世界的保险：重置回出生点
112		if global_position.y < -20.0:
113			global_position = _spawn_pos
114			velocity = Vector3.ZERO
115			return
116	
117		if not is_on_floor():
118			velocity.y -= _gravity * delta
119	
120		if Input.is_action_just_pressed("jump") and is_on_floor():
121			velocity.y = jump_velocity
122	
123		# 获取移动输入（x: 左右, y: 前后），并按身体朝向转为世界方向
124		var input_dir := Input.get_vector("move_left", "move_right", "move_forward", "move_back")
125		var direction := (transform.basis * Vector3(input_dir.x, 0.0, input_dir.y)).normalized()
126		if direction:
127			velocity.x = direction.x * move_speed
128			velocity.z = direction.z * move_speed
129		else:
130			velocity.x = move_toward(velocity.x, 0.0, move_speed)
131			velocity.z = move_toward(velocity.z, 0.0, move_speed)
132	
133		move_and_slide()
134
```

```json
225	func _process(delta: float) -> void:
226		if _hand_attach == null:
227			return
228		# 腕骨当前姿态（骨架局部）→ 相对待机的增量 → 增益放大 → 回到相机空间
229		var cur_local: Transform3D = _rig.global_transform.affine_inverse() * _hand_attach.global_transform
230		if _has_ref:
231			# 位移：绕待机手位放大；旋转：增量转成轴角，角度乘增益（带上限）后叠加基准
232			var rp := _ref_local.origin
233			var new_pos := rp + (cur_local.origin - rp) * POS_GAIN
234			var cur_b := _norm_basis(cur_local.basis)
235			var d := Transform3D(cur_b * _ref_local.basis.inverse(), Vector3.ZERO)
236			var q := d.basis.get_rotation_quaternion()
237			var half := acos(clampf(absf(q.w), 0.0, 1.0))
238			var ang := half * 2.0
239			var new_basis: Basis
240			if ang < 0.001:
241				new_basis = _ref_local.basis
242			else:
243				var ax := Vector3(q.x, q.y, q.z) / sin(half)
244				new_basis = Basis(ax, minf(ang * ROT_GAIN, 3.0)) * _ref_local.basis
245			cur_local = Transform3D(new_basis, new_pos)
246		var hb := cur_local.basis
247		hb = Basis(hb.x.normalized(), hb.y.normalized(), hb.z.normalized())
248		global_transform = Transform3D(hb, cur_local.origin) * HAND_CORRECTION
249		global_transform = _rig.global_transform * global_transform
250		if _attacking:
251			_record_and_draw_trails(delta)
252			_check_hit_timing()

255	func _check_hit_timing() -> void:
256		if _hit_emitted or _anim_player == null:
257			return
258		var cur := _anim_player.current_animation
259		if cur != SLASH_ANIM:
260			return
261		var anim: Animation = _anim_player.get_animation(SLASH_ANIM)
262		if anim == null:
263			return
264		if _anim_player.get_current_animation_position() >= anim.length * 0.35:

269	func _record_and_draw_trails(delta: float) -> void:
270		# 记录剑相对相机的局部姿态（视角旋转不影响残影贴合）
271		_hist.push_front(transform)
272		if _hist.size() > 60:
273			_hist.resize(60)
274		var fps_mult: float = maxf(1.0, 1.0 / maxf(delta, 0.0005))
275		for i in TRAIL_COUNT:
276			var lag_frames: int = int(round(float(i + 1) * TRAIL_DELAY * fps_mult))
277			lag_frames = clampi(lag_frames, 1, _hist.size() - 1)
278			var tr: Transform3D = _hist[lag_frames]
279			# 残影中心对齐刃身中点（刃相对剑柄 -0.31~-0.40）
280			_trails[i].transform = Transform3D(tr.basis, tr.origin + tr.basis * Vector3(0, 0, -0.36))
281			_trails[i].visible = true

285		for c in n.get_children():
286			if c.get_class() == cls:
287				return c
288			var r := _find_node(c, cls)
289			if r != null:
290				return r
291		return null

296		for c in n.get_children():
297			if c.get_class() == cls:
298				out.append(c)
299			out.append_array(_find_nodes(c, cls))
300		return out
```

#### Thinking

Next, let's check main.tscn and HUD, and look at the project settings input map. Also, let's check which files exist.

Plan:
1. Create bow.gd — a procedural bow weapon (view model) attached under Camera3D:
   - Long-press LMB to charge (蓄力), aiming? "长按鼠标左键射击瞄准松手发射" — hold left mouse button to aim/shoot, release to fire. 3 seconds until full charge. Attack power 50. Distance calculated by physics engine (arrow is a RigidBody3D projectile with gravity).
   - Display charge UI (a growing progress, either a Label3D near the crosshair via HUD or draw in a small Control). The simplest is: the bow itself emits a charge_changed signal, and HUD displays the charge bar. Or render a ring. Let's add a charge bar UI element to the HUD.
2. Weapon switching: Z key to toggle between main (sword) and sub (bow). Player or weapon manager handles it: both are children of Camera3D; toggle visibility/enabled.
   - Note: the sword's rig is added to get_parent() (the camera) — when the sword is hidden, the rig skeleton continues animating but the sword's visuals are hidden. Better approach: disable the script and hide all nodes.
   - Also X key attack — should only work when sword is active; LMB shooting only when bow is active.
3. Arrow projectile: RigidBody3D with a mesh (shaft + tip + fletching), initial velocity based on charge (0→full in 3 seconds); damage 50 (full charge? "攻击力50" — attack power 50). Probably damage scales with charge, max 50? The spec says "三秒蓄力满距离按物理引擎算攻击力50" — full charge in 3 seconds, distance determined by physics, attack power 50. My interpretation: full charge = damage 50, less charge = lower damage/velocity. Damage scales linearly from about 10 at minimum to 50 at full charge; full charge gives maximum velocity; flight distance depends on physics (gravity, aim angle). Or fixed at 50. Hmm, "攻击力50" is probably full charge damage 50. Let's do damage = round(lerp(15, 50, charge)) with charge 0..1, and note this. Actually, to be safe against the spec: attack power 50 at full charge. Faster release = lower power. This matches "三秒蓄力满".

   Hit detection: the arrow is a RigidBody with a CollisionShape; on body_entered or via intersect with raycast, if the collider is in the "boss" group → take_damage. Simple approach: attach a script to the arrow: on contact with a body in the "boss" group, deal damage, then stick/despawn. Use max_contacts_reported.

   Also ground collision: stop and fade out, despawn after a few seconds. Total arrow count should be limited (e.g., pool or just delete after a few seconds).

4. Aiming: while holding, could zoom the FOV (aim). "射击瞄准" — hold LMB to aim. Implementation: while holding LMB and bow is equipped, gradually lower FOV from 75 to 50 for aiming, show crosshair. Mouse rotation continues to work.

5. HUD: charge bar. Let's check hud.gd.

```json
129				# 低谷深绿 → 山脊浅黄
130				var col := Color(0.14 + 0.38 * t, 0.26 + 0.38 * t, 0.10 + 0.22 * t)

132		img.resize(int(minimap_size.x), int(minimap_size.y), Image.INTERPOLATE_NEAREST)
```

#### Thinking

Design:

1. **weapons.gd** (manager) — or more simply: put switch logic on the player. Create a small weapon manager on the player: children of Camera3D: Sword, Bow. Z key toggles active weapon. Toggle is done via `set_process_unhandled_input` and `set_visible_in_tree(false)`, disabling the node and setting `process_mode`… Note: the sword's rig is a sibling (added to camera via get_parent()). When the sword is disabled: sword.visible=false hides itself and its children (the sword mesh's nodes are children of the sword node). The rig is added to the camera, not to the sword — the rig is hidden anyway (MeshInstance is hidden). Trails are children of the camera! _build_trails adds to parent (camera). If the sword is inactive, we need to hide the trails — but trails are only shown while _attacking; if the sword's _process is disabled no updates occur; trails may remain visible from the last swing. When the sword is disabled: also, since they're children of the camera, hide the trails. Simplest approach: in sword.gd add `func set_active(a)`, hide self + trails and set process state. Or in the manager: iterate over children of camera whose names match _sword_trail_. Make trails named "SwordTrail%d" and have the manager hide them.

Actually a simpler and cleaner way: the manager toggles `node.enabled` and the weapon side implements set_enabled? Let's design:

weapons.gd (Node3D under Camera3D? no — put the manager on Player or Main). Simplest approach: the manager is player.gd itself: hold references to the sword and bow, Z key toggle. Sword is currently at Camera3D/Sword. Add Bow node at Camera3D/Bow with bow.gd script.

Toggle logic in player.gd's _unhandled_input: KEY_Z → _switch_weapon(). What does:
- _weapon_idx 0=sword, 1=bow.
- sword.visible = (i==0); sword.set_process_unhandled_input(i==0); sword.set_process(i==0)?? Note: when _process is disabled during an attack the animation pauses mid-way; it's better to block switching during attacks, or just interrupt: since nodes are hidden when the sword is disabled it's fine; the rig's animation keeps playing (the AnimationPlayer is on the rig and remains active). When re-enabled, _process resumes. Edge cases are tolerable. Also hide trails on disable: handle with sword.set_active(false) which hides self and trails and clears history.
- bow.set_active similarly.
- Also when switching, if the bow is charging → cancel.

The bow script handles LMB press: only when mouse is captured? Left click when mouse is uncaptured is used to re-capture. The bow's charge should only start when Input.mouse_mode == CAPTURED. And when the bow is equipped and holding LMB → aiming (lower FOV, show crosshair). Player's existing handler in _unhandled_input captures mouse on left click; if mouse is visible the bow shouldn't charge; order: both receive events. Guard with mouse_mode.

2. **bow.gd** design:
- Procedural bow model: recurve bow limbs (torus arc or curve using CylinderMesh segments), grip, string (thin cylinder), no scope. Position at lower right when idle; when aiming (charging), move to center-screen (right hand at cheek, bow vertical slightly left of center). Use Tween for aim transitions.
- Charge: on LMB press (captured, active) start holding: charge_time accumulates, clamp at 3s with 0..1. While charging: pull the arrow nock back (arrow moves from forward of grip toward the right of the grip), string follows (scale/move string node), crosshair shrinks, FOV lerps from 75→48 (aim zoom), HUD shows charge bar (progress %).
- On release: fire arrow: spawn an Arrow RigidBody3D instance at camera's forward position with velocity = direction * lerp(v_min, v_max, charge). v_max ~ 55 m/s, v_min ~ 18. Damage = int(lerp(10, 50, charge))? Per spec "attack power 50" full charge=50. Use base 15 at charge 0 up to 50. Hmm, to follow the wording: full charge 50. Let's do damage = round(lerpf(15.0, 50.0, charge)). Actually simply: attack power = 50 * charge… a zero-charge shot would do 0. Minimum 10. Damage scales from 10 → 50 and we'll document that.
- Arrow: RigidBody3D, submesh of CylinderMesh (shaft 0.02 radius 0.7m) + cone tip + fletching, CollisionShape cylinder. continuous_cd = true. max_contacts_reported=4, contact_monitor=true. On body_entered: if the other body is in group "boss" → boss.take_damage(dmg); spawn a small effect? Then free after sticking (set freeze? just queue_free with a delay). If terrain — does the ground have collision? Ground uses PlaneMesh with… wait, terrain collision: from memory ConcavePolygonShape3D of 51200 faces; so the arrow will collide with the terrain concave. Fine. Despawn: after hit or after lifetime 8s, queue_free. Also add an ArrowGroup "arrows" with a max-cap count (delete the oldest when >20).
- Physics: gravity applies → distance depends on speed and angle (parabolic), so "distance is computed by physics engine" ✓.
- Also hide bow… arrow spawns at camera position + forward*0.3 + right*0.1.

- HUD charge bar: add a Control in hud.gd that listens to the bow? Simpler: bow renders a progress arc via HUD signal. Or use HealthBarXControl with a second bar for charge below the HP bar! Already a vector-drawn bar. Add a "charge bar" width 160 with yellow/orange color, value 0-100, hidden unless charging. HUD connects to bow's signals: charge_changed(float 0..1). HUD finds Bow node and connects.

- Crosshair: draw a simple Control with _draw on the bow? Can be added to HUD too. Let's add a small crosshair: 4 lines + center dot as ColorRect in HUD, shown when bow is active. Keep the scope: bow emits charge_changed; HUD shows charge bar + crosshair.

Simplify further: bow.gd creates its own CanvasLayer? The HUD approach is cleaner. Implementation:
- bow.gd signals: charge_started(charge), charge_updated(charge: float), shot_released(charge) → HUD hides the bar.
Actually even simpler: expose `func get_charge() -> float` and `is_charging()`; HUD polls the bow node every frame in _process: if charging, show bar, set value; else hide bar. And show crosshair when bow is active: poll `bow.active`. HUD finds the camera's Bow node: `../Player/Camera3D/Bow`.

3. **Sword changes**:
- KEY_X only attacks when sword is active → guard with `active` flag; manager sets via `set_active()`.
- Add `var active := true`; in _unhandled_input: if not active: return.
- set_active(a): active=a; visible=a; if(!a): hide trails, clear hist, _attacking=false, stop? Also leave animation as idle. When a==false don't update transform → when re-enabled it snaps. Fine.
- Trails are children of camera: hide them on deactivate.
- Also the bow holds a "primary/secondary weapon" concept: primary sword, secondary bow, toggled with Z. Should we display a label indicating the current weapon? Add a HUD text "Current weapon: Sword/Bow (Z to switch)" below the coordinates. Nice touch, small effort: HUD polls bow.active.

4. **player.gd changes**:
- In _ready find sword and bow, store them, initial value _weapon=0.
- Z key: toggle sword/bow with _switch_weapon().
- slash_hit handler unchanged (sword only fires when active).
- Bow shot hit detection: handled in the arrow script itself (body_entered). Arrow needs damage on the boss.

5. **main.tscn**: add Bow Node3D with bow.gd script under Camera3D. Bump load_steps to 14, ext_resource id 12_bow.

Arrow scene: create scripts/arrow.gd, build the arrow at runtime in bow.gd (no separate tscn needed). RigidBody3D built in code: mesh via a SurfaceTool from a merged CylinderMesh+cone? Even easier: RigidBody with a child MeshInstance3D CylinderMesh (rotated 90° on X to align axis along -Z), plus a child cone tip, fletching box; CollisionShape3D CylinderShape rotated similarly. The RigidBody needs its proper center of mass; the default body_with_centroid_force… add an `arrow.gd` script to the RigidBody handling body_entered and lifetime, with fields `dmg`, `owner`.

Note: RigidBody3D needs custom_integrator? No, the default is fine. Apply velocity with `linear_velocity` after add_child. gravity_scale default 1 → parabolic. Fast arrow + thin concave terrain → tunneling risk: set `continuous_cd` to true (motion-safe margin?). In Godot 4: `continuous_cd = true`, `max_collisions_with_velocity`? There's the property `max_contacts_reported`, `contact_monitor`, and CCD via `physics_material_override`? Actually RigidBody3D has a property `continuous_cd` (float? bool). Godot 4: `RigidBody3D.continuous_cd: bool`. Yes. Also can do raycast on body_entered for precise hit location, not needed; damage on body_entered works.

Boss StaticBody3D collision layer: which layer? Check the collision layer setup in boss.gd. Player ray queries use default mask 1. Arrow's collision_mask default 1 hits the boss (layer 1?) and ground (layer?). terrain.gd's collision — probably default layer 1. Fine, defaults all work.

Also mouse handling: bow._unhandled_input receives InputEventMouseButton for button_index LEFT. Press → start charge (if active, mouse captured, not dead). Release → fire. Also prevent conflict with player's "click to re-capture": if mouse is visible, the player captures; the bow guards on captured so no charge. Good.

Aiming FOV: camera.fov lerp; the bow needs the camera reference = get_parent(). On deactivation while charging, restore FOV.

View bob? Skip.

Also the sword currently processes the KEY_X handler; add active guard.

Let's check the boss.gd group and collision layer.

Arrow spawn function:
```gdscript
static func spawn(xform: Transform3D, velocity: Vector3, damage: int, world: Node) -> Node:
    # Clean up too many arrows
    var stale: Array = []
    for a in _active:
        if is_instance_valid(a): stale.append(a)
    _active = stale
    while _active.size() >= MAX_ALIVE:
        _active.pop_front().queue_free()   # pop_front returns the removed element
        ... then re-sync _active
```
Careful: queue_free'd nodes remain valid until end of frame; guard by removing from _active in _exit_tree.

Strand update in _process:
```
func _strand_transform(a: Vector3, b: Vector3) -> Transform3D:
    var y := b - a
    var len := y.length()
    if len < 0.0001: return Transform3D()
    var yn := y / len
    var ref := Vector3(1,0,0) if absf(yn.y) < 0.9 else Vector3(0,0,1)
    var x := ref.cross(yn).normalized()
    var z := x.cross(yn)
    return Transform3D(Basis(x, yn * len, z), (a + b) * 0.5)
```
Basis(x, ycol, z) constructor takes 3 vectors as columns. Yes.

Title extraction failed (regex issue due to data-react-helmet or line breaks). Not a big deal — just download a few of the candidate arrow GLBs and inspect them with Python's gltf JSON parsing (mesh names, vertex counts, dimensions). Quaternius's "Arrows" model name should appear in the mesh names within the GLB. Let's download all 12 to a scratch directory in the workspace and parse the gltf JSON chunks (mesh names + AABB from accessors).

#### Tool: Bash

```bash
python - <<'PY'
import struct, json, os, urllib.request, tempfile
urls={
"bC3FokNqTpi":"87102856-23f4-4788-9788-372b90587dec",
"5Qfnyb5ugK0":"da4c6160-5681-47a4-8906-f80f3bfe7b2a",
"Rt48KEPDGt":"5af9e305-e42c-4f87-a033-28261fdaa3a4",
"ebdNfNmww_7":"ebd38606-cd45-4f94-9bfd-5a9da76e72aa",
"1TUCDmHZKQY":"7e24b237-8c48-41c7-a760-c6272b0ba3ee",
"8xde5IVnRR_":"34c8f317-e941-4605-a309-01671d80f73a",
"6pMBOmBFxGt":"443bb266-3c74-43a1-998b-7b54ad9a8e5f",
"dwmvPHHCdq":"8f3134c7-f206-41e1-9c67-55f3fe566490",
"43TYiGXodkM":"4e13bc38-bdba-48c8-81f5-7d2994305220",
"40NyZvZPvQT":"62212189-1f5e-44fd-a338-69829c50e176",
"coE6b0yp-P6":"bbc864cd-c5fa-490d-9aaa-99eabf8876c2",
}
d=os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(),"arrowscan"); os.makedirs(d,exist_ok=True)
hdr={"User-Agent":"Mozilla/5.0 Chrome/126"}
def meta(name):
    b=open(name,'rb').read()
    ln,ty=struct.unpack_from('<II',b,12)
    j=json.loads(b[20:20+ln])
    meshes=[m.get('name','?') for m in j.get('meshes',[])]
    acs=j.get('accessors',[])
    # AABB via POSITION accessors of accessors of primitives
    aabb=[]
    try:
        for m in j.get('meshes',[]):
            for p in m.get('primitives',[]):
                pa=acs[p['attributes']['POSITION']]
                if 'min' in pa: aabb.append((pa['min'],pa['max']))
    except Exception: pass
    verts=sum(acs[p['attributes']['POSITION']]['count'] for m in j.get('meshes',[]) for p in m.get('primitives',[]))
    return meshes, verts, aabb, len(b)
for k,u in urls.items():
    fp=os.path.join(d,k+".glb")
    try:
        urllib.request.urlretrieve(f"https://static.poly.pizza/{u}.glb",fp)
        ms,v,ab,sz=meta(fp)
        rng=[f"{round(max(mx[0]-mn[0],mx[1]-mn[1],mx[2]-mn[2]),2)}" for mn,mx in ab[:2]]
        print(k,"size",sz,"verts",v,"meshes",ms[:4],"maxdim",rng)
    except Exception as e:
        print(k,"ERR",e)
PY
```

#### Thinking

The structure is clear:
- bow_raw.glb: surf0 = wooden bow body (498 vertices, Y is vertical at 4.76, X is depth 0.9), surf1 = gray grip (144 vertices, small box near center at x -0.38..-0.18), surf2 = "Line" = bowstring (24 vertices, flat at x≈0.47, Y spans ±2.34). So the bowstring is at x=+0.47 plane, and the bow curves toward negative x. The string is a straight vertical line at x=0.47.
- arrow.glb: single mesh, shaft is along X axis (length 2.17, X is -0.82 to 1.35), thickness Y 0.04, Z 0.24 (fletching). Has texture.

Plan for bow.gd view model:
- Instantiate the bow glb, get the MeshInstance3D, rebuild the ArrayMesh with only surf0+surf1 (body+grip), exclude surf2 (string). Then procedurally add 2 string strands connecting the nock point (nocked position) to the tips. The tips are approximately (0.47, ±2.34, 0) in the model's local space.
- Scale: model height 4.76 → want about 1.1m → scale 0.23.
- Orientation: model: bow is vertical Y, string plane at x=+0.47, bow bends toward -x. In camera space, the bow is held vertical (Y up), string faces the player (+Z toward the camera), arrow is fired in -Z direction. Arrow direction: along the model's X axis → rotate the model so X→-Z: rotation Y = +90°? Rotating -90 around Y axis maps X→? RotY(θ): x' = x cosθ + z sinθ. Vector (1,0,0) under RotY(90°) → (cos90, 0, -sin90)=(0,0,-1). So rotation.y=90° maps model X (arrow direction) to camera -Z (forward). Then the string plane at x=0.47 → maps to z=-0.47 (forward). Good: string at the front, grip pulled toward the shooter... wait, the grip is at x -0.38..-0.18 → z +0.09..0.18, pulled toward the shooter. Consistent with drawing: nock pulled back along +Z.

But actually the arrow is nocked at the string and passes through the side of the grip. No problem.

So the bow root node: rotation_degrees (0, 90, 0) + scale 0.23; then the string's local endpoints: tip_u = (0, 2.34, -0.47)*0.23 → in the rotated frame... it's easier to define the string in the same rotated parent space: create a _root with rotation Y=90 and scale, and inside it put a "ModelPivot" with the rebuilt mesh, and a "StringSpace" node with no rotation (local axes = model axes: X forward→? no wait: children of _root inherit its rotation; the string endpoints are specified in model coordinates: tip_u=(0.47, 2.34, 0), tip_l=(0.47,-2.34,0), nock=(z_nock... in model coordinates, the string is pulled in the -x direction (grip is at -x, pulled further back): nock=(0.47 - draw, 0, 0), draw is 0→about 1.6 model units (0.37m). Arrow visual: instantiate arrow.glb (shaft is along X axis, tip at +1.35 side? Tip is probably the +X end (max 1.35); fletching is the -0.82 end). Arrow nock position = nock point; arrow extends in +X direction: center position = nock_x + about 0.26 (half the length of 2.17). Set _nocked as a container, position.x = nock_x, child arrow mesh offset x=+0.27.

Model scale 0.23: string draw distance 1.6*0.23=0.37m — reasonable.

String strands: unit-height cylinder, radius 0.004 (model units, then scaled by parent... if strands are children of a node scaled 0.23, the cylinder radius is in model units: radius 0.02 model units → 4.6mm. Use 0.025.)

For simplicity, place the string/arrow nodes as children of the scaled+rotated _root, so everything is in model coordinates.

But note: non-uniform... scale is uniform 0.23, no problem.

Arrow projectile (world): instantiate arrow.glb mesh under a RigidBody3D; the mesh is rotated so the shaft's X axis → -Z (forward): rotation_degrees (0,-90,0)? RotY(-90): (1,0,0)→(cos(-90),0,-sin(-90))=(0,0,1)=+Z backward. RotY(+90) gives → -Z forward. So the mesh node's rotation.y=90, scale about 0.35 (arrow 2.17→0.76m).
```gdscript
extends RigidBody3D
## Arrow projectile: physics engine handles gravity parabola, range/trajectory determined by initial velocity (charge level) and angle.
## On collision with BOSS, subtract HP based on charge damage; arrow sticks in place then disappears after a delay.

const ARROW_MODEL := preload("res://assets/weapons/arrow.glb")
const MAX_ALIVE := 15

static var _active: Array = []

var dmg := 50
var _hit := false
var _life := 0.0


## Spawn an arrow from the camera muzzle: orient along view direction and give initial velocity (damage is calculated externally based on charge)
static func spawn(parent: Node, cam_basis: Basis, origin: Vector3, speed: float, damage: int) -> void:
	_prune()
	while _active.size() >= MAX_ALIVE:
		var old: Node = _active.pop_front()
		if is_instance_valid(old):
			old.queue_free()
	var ar: RigidBody3D = load("res://scripts/arrow.gd").new()
	ar.dmg = damage
	ar._configure()
	parent.add_child(ar)
	ar.global_transform = Transform3D(cam_basis.orthonormalized(), origin)
	ar.linear_velocity = -cam_basis.z * speed
	_active.append(ar)


static func _prune() -> void:
	var live: Array = []
	for a in _active:
		if is_instance_valid(a):
			live.append(a)
	_active = live
```

_on_body_entered(other: Node) -> void:
```
	if _hit:
		return
	_hit = true
	if other != null and other.is_in_group("boss"):
		var boss := other.get_parent()
		if boss != null and boss.has_method("take_damage"):
			boss.take_damage(dmg)
	freeze = true
	contact_monitor = false

```
Note: does is_in_group also include the boss's Node3D root? The root is also added to the group ("boss" group is on both root and StaticBody). The collision body that gets hit is the StaticBody3D (in group) → get_parent() = boss root → take_damage. But the root is also in the group, and get_parent of root = Main, which doesn't have take_damage → has_method false → no damage. To be safe, walk up:
```
var n: Node = other
while n != null and not (n.has_method("take_damage") and n.is_in_group("boss")):
	n = n.get_parent()
```
Simpler: if other.is_in_group("boss"): var n=other; while n and not n.has_method("take_damage"): n=n.get_parent(); if n: n.take_damage(dmg).

```
func _fire() -> void:
	var norm := clampf(_charge / CHARGE_TIME, 0.0, 1.0)
	var speed := lerpf(SPEED_MIN, SPEED_MAX, norm)
	var damage := int(round(lerpf(float(DMG_MIN), float(DMG_MAX), norm)))
	_charging = false
	_charge = 0.0
	if _camera == null:
		return
	var g := _camera.global_transform
	var fwd := -g.basis.z.normalized()
	var origin := g.origin + fwd * 0.45 + g.basis.x * 0.06
	var scene := get_tree().current_scene
	if scene == null:
		scene = get_tree().root
	ARROW_SCRIPT.spawn(scene, g.basis, origin, speed, damage)
```

_strand_xform:
```
func _strand_xform(a: Vector3, b: Vector3) -> Transform3D:
	var y := b - a
	var ln := y.length()
	if ln < 0.0001:
		return Transform3D()
	var yn := y / ln
	var ref := Vector3(0, 0, 1) if absf(yn.y) < 0.9 else Vector3(1, 0, 0)
	var x := ref.cross(yn).normalized()
	var z := x.cross(yn)
	return Transform3D(Basis(x, y, z), (a + b) * 0.5)
```
Basis(x, y, z) — the constructor takes 3 basis vectors (columns). Non-uniform scaling in the y column stretches the unit cylinder.

```gdscript
extends SceneTree

var _scene: Node
var _t := 0.0

func _initialize() -> void:
	_scene = load("res://scenes/main.tscn").instantiate()
	root.add_child(_scene)
	_run()

func _run() -> void:
	await process_frame
	await process_frame
	var player = _scene.get_node("Player")
	var cam = player.get_node("Camera3D")
	var sword = cam.get_node("Sword")
	var bow = cam.get_node("Bow")
	var boss = _scene.get_node("Boss")
	# Face toward the boss
	var d: Vector3 = boss.global_position - player.global_position
	player.rotation.y = atan2(-d.x, -d.z)
	print("DIST %.1f" % d.length())
	print("T1 sword.active=", sword.active, " bow.active=", bow.active)
	_press_key(KEY_Z)
	await process_frame
	await process_frame
	print("T2 after Z: sword.active=", sword.active, " bow.active=", bow.active, " bow.visible=", bow.visible)
	# Half charge
	_press_lmb(true)
	await create_timer(1.2).timeout
	print("T3 charging=", bow.is_charging(), " ratio=%.2f" % bow.charge_ratio())
	root.get_texture().get_image().save_png("C:/Users/xiaomi.h/.qwenworkcn/workspace/mt9ivdjpdp3ogfvg/snap/bow_half.png")
	await create_timer(2.0).timeout
	print("T4 full ratio=%.2f" % bow.charge_ratio())
	root.get_texture().get_image().save_png(".../bow_full.png")
	var hp_before: float = boss.hp
	_press_lmb(false)
```

Helpers:
```
func _press_key(k: int) -> void:
	var e := InputEventKey.new()
	e.keycode = k as Key
	e.pressed = true
	Input.parse_input_event(e)
	var u := InputEventKey.new()
	u.keycode = k as Key
	u.pressed = false
	Input.parse_input_event(u)

func _press_lmb(down: bool) -> void:
	var e := InputEventMouseButton.new()
	e.button_index = MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT
	e.pressed = down
	Input.parse_input_event(e)
```

The bigger issue is in `_on_body_entered` — I'm setting `contact_monitor = false` directly, which throws an error and might leave the monitor in a broken state. I should defer that instead.

The string is on the model's +X side; the string should be on the player's side (world +Z relative to the bow). So model +X → world +Z. That's rotY(90): rotY(θ) maps local X to (cosθ,0,-sinθ). For local X → world +Z we need cosθ=0, -sinθ=1 → θ=-90. So _bow_space rotation (0,-90,0) maps model +X → world... let me compute: rotY(-90): x-axis=(cos(-90),0,-sin(-90))=(0,0,1)=world +Z. #### Thinking

The `$_` in PowerShell got mangled by bash (I used $_ without escaping it). Known pitfall in memory: in the Bash tool, `$p` inside `powershell -Command` with double quotes gets swallowed by bash, so you need to write it as `\$p`. I wrote `$_.ProcessName` without escaping. Let me redo it with proper escaping, or use a simpler check: `tasklist | grep -i exe` — but the exe name is in Chinese, and the encoding of the tasklist output is GBK. Use `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq 游戏大乱斗.exe"`? The bash→cmd argument encoding for Chinese might work. Or, write the PS command out to a temporary .ps1 file... The simplest is: escape `$_` and use PowerShell.

命令里 `$_` 被 bash 吞了（已知坑）。转义重查。



#### Tool: Bash

```bash
powershell -Command "Get-Process | Where-Object {\$_.Path -like 'E:\*\build\*' -or \$_.ProcessName -match '9b1f' } | Select-Object Id,ProcessName | Format-Table -HideTableHeaders" ; powershell -Command "[Console]::OutputEncoding=[Text.Encoding]::UTF8; (Get-Process | Where-Object {\$_.MainModule.FileName -like 'E:\*' } | Select-Object -First 5 Id,ProcessName) | Out-String" 2>/dev/null | head -8
```

#### Thinking

The first query returned nothing (no process with a Path under E:\...\build\ exists) — meaning the game exe isn't running. Either it crashed on startup, or the earlier background launch failed. Note: the exe was launched with `--path "E:\游戏大乱斗"` — actually, for an exported exe, the --path argument is unnecessary and might even be harmful? The exported game embeds the pck; passing --path pointing to the project directory is fine (it was used in the launcher). But the earlier smoke test: launched with `&`, then checked with sleep 8 — grep failed due to an encoding issue; then this check shows it's not running now. It may have crashed. Let's launch it in the background and get the exit code/output.

#### Thinking

--write-movie /dev/null got broken (cmd's redirection). exit=127... let's do it more simply: run the exe in the background, sleep, check the process by window title with a tasklist filter, then kill it. Use PowerShell's Start-Process + Get-Process by name.

#### Tool: Bash

```bash
powershell -Command "Start-Process -FilePath 'E:\游戏大乱斗\build\游戏大乱斗.exe'; Start-Sleep -Seconds 12; \$p = Get-Process | Where-Object {\$_.Path -eq 'E:\游戏大乱斗\build\游戏大乱斗.exe'}; if(\$p){ 'RUNNING pid='+\$p.Id; Stop-Process -Id \$p.Id } else { 'NOT RUNNING' }"
```

**Output:**

```json
RUNNING pid=2632
```

The exported exe is working. Next, rebuild the share zip (exe + 玩法説明.txt). Use Compress-Archive. After that, clean up smoke.log (inside the build directory — delete it).

#### Thinking

The reason the rm -f smoke.log command failed is that the current directory (cwd) resolution is... the error message is in Chinese: "删除目标不明确 (deletion target is ambiguous)" — is this because the file protection policy is blocking rm? Actually, this error looks like it's from the sandbox: rm is prohibited in user directories (file protection). Exactly right — rm is forbidden in user zones. smoke.log is inside E:\游戏大乱斗\build (a user directory). Use the recycle bin method instead. Also, the reason Compress-Archive didn't run was because it was chained after rm? I used `;` after rm..., but the error occurred at the rm stage, and the whole thing failed? The output only shows the deletion error. Let's run them separately: send smoke.log to the recycle bin, then compress.

#### Tool: Bash

```bash
powershell -Command "if(Test-Path 'E:\游戏大乱斗\build\smoke.log'){Add-Type -AssemblyName Microsoft.VisualBasic; [Microsoft.VisualBasic.FileIO.FileSystem]::DeleteFile('E:\游戏大乱斗\build\smoke.log','OnlyErrorDialogs','SendToRecycleBin')}; Compress-Archive -Path 'E:\游戏大乱斗\build\游戏大乱斗.exe','E:\游戏大乱斗\build\玩法说明.txt' -DestinationPath 'E:\游戏大乱斗\build\野生狗奶大乱斗_分享包.zip' -CompressionLevel Optimal -Force" && ls -la "E:\游戏大乱斗\build"
```

弓箭和主副武器机制做好了，全部按"找现成资源"的思路实现：

**资源来源**：先用浏览器查了 Godot 官方素材库，搜 "bow" 只有 2D 插件和脚本（Crossbow/Animated Bow 都不是 3D 模型），于是用了 Poly Pizza 的 CC0 3D 模型——弓（Zsky）和箭（Quaternius，Ultimate RPG 包），和之前挥剑动捕的 king.glb 同源，免登录直链下载、可商用免署名，来源清单存在 `assets/weapons/CREDITS.txt`。

**机制实现**
- 主/副武器：初始主武器剑，按 **Z** 切换剑 ↔ 弓（HUD 有当前武器提示，切走时蓄力自动取消、视野恢复）
- 弓箭：按住鼠标左键瞄准（视野从 75° 拉近到 48°），弓身移到眼前、弦随蓄力后拉、箭搭在弦上；**3 秒蓄满**，底部出现蓄力条 + 屏幕准星；松手发射

```json
func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:

		return
	if event is InputEventMouseButton and event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT:
		if event.pressed:
			if Input.mouse_mode == Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED and _cooldown <= 0.0:
				_charging = true
				_charge = 0.0
		else:
			if _charging:
				_fire()
...
```

Star texture generation in GDScript:
```
func _star_texture() -> ImageTexture:
	var s := 32
	var img := Image.create(s, s, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
	img.fill(Color(0,0,0,0))
	var c := s/2.0
	for y in s:
		for x in s:
			var dx := (x-c+0.5)/c; var dy := (y-c+0.5)/c
			# 4-point star: |dx|+|dy| + k*sqrt? Use superellipse-style: r = (|dx|^p + |dy|^p)... 4-point star: (|x|+|y|) + a*(x²+y²)??
			# Simple: 4-point star condition: (abs(dx)+abs(dy) <= 1) and (dx²+dy² >= something)? That gives a diamond with a hole.
			# Classic 4-point star: |dx|*|dy| <= 0.06 and abs(dx)+abs(dy)<=1 → thin cross arms
			var v := 0.0
			if absf(dx*dy) < 0.045 and abs(dx)+abs(dy) < 1.0: v = 1.0 - (abs(dx)+abs(dy))
			if dx*dx+dy*dy < 0.09: v = maxf(v, 1.0 - sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy)*2.6)
			if v > 0: img.set_pixel(x, y, Color(1, 0.95, 0.6, clampf(v*1.4,0,1)))
	return ImageTexture.create_from_image(img)
```

```json
	## 32x32 四角星：十字星芒 + 亮芯，边缘渐隐
	var s := 32
	var img := Image.create(s, s, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)

	var c := s * 0.5
	for y in s:

			var dy := (y - c + 0.5) / c
			var v := 0.0

			if v > 0.0:

	return ImageTexture.create_from_image(img)
```

```json
# ---- 攻击前摇状态机：待机 → 蓄力（星点逐渐增多）→ 蓄满保持（攻击占位）----
func _update_windup(delta: float) -> void:
	_phase_t += delta
	_orbit += delta * (2.2 + 4.0 * clampf(float(_phase_t) / CHARGE_TIME, 0.0, 1.0) * float(_phase == 1))
	match _phase:
		0:
			_hide_stars()
			if _phase_t >= CHARGE_GAP:
				_phase = 1
				_phase_t = 0.0
		1:
			var prog := clampf(_phase_t / CHARGE_TIME, 0.0, 1.0)
			# 蓄力进度越高，点亮的星点越多
			var lit := int(prog * float(MAX_STARS))
			for i in MAX_STARS:
				_stars[i].visible = i < lit
			_layout_stars(prog)
			# 蓄力震颤
			_visual.position.x = 0.06 * sin(_t * 34.0) * prog
			if _phase_t >= CHARGE_TIME:
				_phase = 2
				_phase_t = 0.0
		2:
			# 蓄满：全部星点高速环绕闪烁（此处将来接攻击释放）
			for i in MAX_STARS:
				_stars[i].visible = (int(_t * 14.0) + i) % 4 != 0
			_layout_stars(1.0)
			_visual.position.x = 0.09 * sin(_t * 44.0)
			if _phase_t >= HOLD_TIME:
				_phase = 0
				_phase_t = 0.0
				_hide_stars()


func _layout_stars(prog: float) -> void:
	## 星点绕身体螺旋环绕：半径随蓄力收缩、高度错开、尺寸微涨
	var n := MAX_STARS
	for i in n:
		var a := _orbit + TAU * float(i) / float(n)
		var radius := lerpf(4.6, 3.0, prog)
		var h := 0.8 + fmod(float(i) * 1.37, 5.6)
		var s: float = _stars[i].scale.x
		var target := lerpf(0.7, 1.25, prog) * (1.0 + 0.12 * sin(_t * 9.0 + float(i)))
		_stars[i].position = Vector3(cos(a) * radius, h, sin(a) * radius)
		_stars[i].scale = Vector3.ONE * lerpf(s, target, 0.2)


func _hide_stars() -> void:
	for st in _stars:
		st.visible = false

```

Let's rewrite the entire state machine. Phase 1 = windup (stars gradually appear, music plays), Phase 2 = attack (boss flies up, sun/moon cycle, damage tick every 0.1 seconds), Phase 3 = landing. Also, we need to handle the boss's global_position.y for flight — but the boss is a Node3D whose position is set by teleport_to. Let's use a child node _flight_pivot, or adjust position.y directly.

Actually, the boss's root position is set by teleport_to to arena center+(0,0,-10). During flight, we want to raise the boss up. But the collision body is a child of the boss. Raising the boss's y will also raise the collision — that's fine (the boss flies up). However, the player's slash raycasts won't reach the high boss — this is acceptable during the invincible attack animation. Actually, should the boss be attackable during flight? The user didn't specify. Let's keep it attackable (the collision moves up with it).

Let's implement the flight by adjusting a separate variable _fly_y and setting position.y = _arena_base_y + _fly_y. But teleport_to sets position. Let's store the base and apply flight in _process.

Actually, the boss's position.y is set to 100.0 by teleport_to (arena center y=100). Wait, teleport_to(center + Vector3(0,0,-10)) → y = 100. And _arena_base_y = position.y = 100. Good. During flight, position.y = _arena_base_y + fly_height.

Let's write the new _process and state machine.

Regarding the sun/moon: the arena's sun is a DirectionalLight3D. Let's add a method to the arena to rotate the sun and switch to moonlight based on a 0..1 parameter. Actually, "sun-moon alternation" = the sun and moon alternate. During the 14-second attack, rotate the sun 360 degrees so day→night→day. Let's add arena.set_day_night(phase01) to rotate the sun's angle and darken the sky at night.

Let's design the arena's day/night:

```json
188		var yn := y / ln

190		var x := ref.cross(yn).normalized()
```

```
func _pick_wander_target() -> void:
	## After skill activation completes: randomly select a new standing point up to 100 steps (units) from current position, clamped within arena
	var ang := randf() * TAU
	var dist := randf() * 100.0
	var t := position + Vector3(cos(ang) * dist, 0.0, sin(ang) * dist)
	var lim := 360.0   # Arena HALF=400, leave margin so we don't stick to the edge
	t.x = clampf(t.x, -lim, lim)
	t.z = clampf(t.z, -lim, lim)
	t.y = _arena_base_y
	_wander_target = t
	_wandering = true
```

_update_wander:
```
func _update_wander(delta: float) -> void:
	if not _wandering:
		return
	var to := _wander_target - position
	to.y = 0.0
	var d := to.length()
	const WANDER_SPEED := 45.0
	if d <= 0.5:
		position.x = _wander_target.x
		position.z = _wander_target.z
		position.y = _arena_base_y
		_wandering = false
		return
	var step := minf(WANDER_SPEED * delta, d)
	position += to.normalized() * step
	position.y = _arena_base_y
```

```json
...


func _hide_stars() -> void:
	for st in _stars:
		st.visible = false


func _pick_wander_target() -> void:
	## 释放完技能后：在当前位置随机选一个最多 100 单位的新落点，夹在场地内
	var ang := randf() * TAU
	var dist := randf() * 100.0
	var t := position + Vector3(cos(ang) * dist, 0.0, sin(ang) * dist)
	var lim := 360.0                 # 场地半宽 400，留 40 边距
	t.x = clampf(t.x, -lim, lim)
	t.z = clampf(t.z, -lim, lim)
	t.y = _arena_base_y
	_wander_target = t
	_wandering = true


func _update_wander(delta: float) -> void:
	if not _wandering:
		return
	var to := _wander_target - position
	to.y = 0.0
	var d := to.length()
	if d <= 0.5:
		position.x = _wander_target.x
		position.z = _wander_target.z
		position.y = _arena_base_y
		_wandering = false
		return
	var step := minf(WANDER_SPEED * delta, d)
	position += to.normalized() * step
	position.y = _arena_base_y

```

```json
151		var ground := get_node_or_null("../Ground")

159			for i in 12:

161				var x := cos(ang) * r
162				var z := sin(ang) * r
163				var h: float = ground.height_at(x, z)
164				if h > best_h:
165					best_h = h
166					best = Vector3(x, h + 2.0, z)
167		return best
```

#### Thinking

Now I understand the movement mechanism. Let's implement the dash.

Dash design (double-tap a direction key to dash):
- Movement actions: "move_forward", "move_back", "move_left", "move_right" (WASD).
- Detect double-tap: when a movement key is pressed (not echo), check if the same action was pressed within DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW (0.3 seconds). If so → dash in that direction.
- Dash: a burst of speed. Set `_dash_time = DASH_DURATION` (e.g., 0.18 seconds) and `_dash_dir` (world direction for that key). During the dash, override horizontal velocity with `_dash_dir * DASH_SPEED`. Add cooldown `_dash_cd` (e.g., 0.5 seconds).

But the dash direction should be relative to the camera/body yaw. For "move_forward" (W), dash forward; S is back; A is left; D is right. Calculate direction from the key:
- forward: -basis.z (body's forward)
- Actually, input_dir maps to (x, y), and direction = basis * (x,0,y). For a single key:
  - move_forward → input_dir.y = -1 (Godot's get_vector: y = forward is negative). direction = basis*(0,0,-1) = body's forward.
  - Let's just calculate the dash direction using the same transform for the tapped key.

Simpler approach: when a double-tap of movement key K is detected, set _dash_dir to the world direction corresponding to K:
  - forward (W): transform.basis * Vector3(0,0,-1)
  - back (S): transform.basis * Vector3(0,0,1)
  - left (A): transform.basis * Vector3(-1,0,0)
  - right (D): transform.basis * Vector3(1,0,0)
Normalize, y=0.

In _physics_process, if _dash_time > 0: velocity.x/z = _dash_dir * DASH_SPEED; decrement _dash_time. Otherwise, normal movement.

Input detection: need to know which movement key was pressed. In _unhandled_input, event is InputEventKey and not echo. Map keycode to direction. But movement uses actions. We can check event.keycode against KEY_W/A/S/D (and arrow keys). Let's handle both WASD and arrow keys.

Actually, a cleaner approach: track key presses with `Input.is_action_just_pressed("move_forward")` etc. inside _physics_process. This avoids keycode mapping and respects the project's action bindings. Double-tap detection: keep a dictionary of last tap times per action; if just_pressed and (now - last) <= window → dash.

But _physics_process runs at the physics rate (default 60Hz), which is sufficient for tap detection (0.3-second window = 18 physics frames). just_pressed works inside _physics_process.

Let's implement in _physics_process:
```
var now := Time.get_ticks_msec() / 1000.0
for each action in [forward, back, left, right]:
    if Input.is_action_just_pressed(action):
        if now - _last_tap.get(action, -99) <= DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW and _dash_cd <= 0:
            _start_dash(action)
        _last_tap[action] = now
```
Wait, but this checks just_pressed for each action every physics frame. No problem.

_start_dash(action): set _dash_dir based on action and body basis; _dash_time = DASH_DURATION; _dash_cd = DASH_COOLDOWN.

Movement:
```
if _dash_time > 0.0:
    _dash_time -= delta
    velocity.x = _dash_dir.x * DASH_SPEED
    velocity.z = _dash_dir.z * DASH_SPEED
else:
    ... normal movement ...
if _dash_cd > 0: _dash_cd -= delta
```

DASH_SPEED: e.g., 16 (about 3x move_speed). DASH_DURATION: 0.18 seconds → about 2.9m per dash. Could go 0.2 seconds and 18 → about 3.6m. Let's go with DASH_SPEED=18, DASH_DURATION=0.2 → about 3.6m burst. Feels snappy.

The health bar label formatting (line 238): `st.label_format.replace("{value}", str(int(roundf(num_val))))`. So it's rounding the value to int for display. Therefore, even if HP is a float like 86.3, the label will display "86/100". Good — no ugly-looking decimals. The bar fill uses the raw float value. So the only HUD changes needed are the signal handler type (int → float) and the initial read type (int → float). In practice, `_on_hp_changed(current: int, _maximum: int)` — when the signal emits a float, a handler typed as int will either error out or truncate. In Godot, if you connect a signal with typed arguments, the handler's signature should match. If the signal is now (float, float) and the handler is (int, int), Godot might throw an error at emit time or at connect time. Let's change the handler to float.

Also, lines 70–71: `var max_hp: int = _player.get("max_hp")` — get returns a float (100.0), and assigning it to an int-typed var → in GDScript 4, does this cause an error? Actually, if it's a whole-number float, GDScript might allow it with a warning? No, it's an error. So we need to change these to float.

```json
func _start_dash(act: String) -> void:
	## 依据被双击的方向键，沿身体朝向的对应水平方向发起一段冲刺
	var d := Vector3.ZERO
	match act:
		"move_forward": d = -transform.basis.z
		"move_back":    d = transform.basis.z
		"move_left":    d = -transform.basis.x
		"move_right":   d = transform.basis.x
	d.y = 0.0
	if d.length_squared() < 0.0001:
		return
	_dash_dir = d.normalized()
	_dash_time = DASH_DURATION
	_dash_cd = DASH_COOLDOWN
```

```json
func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	_t += delta

		# 沉地消失
		_visual.position.y = maxf(_visual.position.y - delta * 1.2, -0.25 * 24.0 * 0.9)

		_visual.rotation.y = lerp_angle(_visual.rotation.y, atan2(d.x, d.z), minf(1.0, delta * 3.0))
	_visual.position.y = 0.12 + 0.1 * sin(_t * 1.4)
	_visual.position.x = 0.0
	if _arena_mode:
```

```json
extends Node3D
## 程序化起伏地形：fbm 高度场生成网格；碰撞用三角网格（ConcavePolygonShape3D）贴合地形。
## 物理体必须在物理帧之后创建，场景加载期创建的碰撞体不会被物理世界接收。

@export var size := 500.0
@export var segments := 128
@export var height_amp := 13.0
@export var frequency := 0.009

const GROUND_SHADER := preload("res://shaders/ground.gdshader")

# 碰撞构建时缓存的高度网格（供 height_at_fast）
var _grid: PackedFloat32Array
var _grid_n := 0
var _grid_half := 0.0
var _grid_cell := 1.0


func _ready() -> void:
	# mesh 立即生成（渲染需要）；物理体延迟到第一个物理帧创建
	_build_terrain_mesh()
	await get_tree().physics_frame
	_build_collision()
	_build_boundary_walls()


# ---- 公共高度查询：草/杂物用它贴合地表 ----
func height_at(x: float, z: float) -> float:
	return _height_at(x, z)


func height_at_fast(x: float, z: float) -> float:
	## 双线性采样缓存高度网格（微秒级），供小地图等概览用途；
	## 网格未就绪（碰撞构建前）时回退解析式。
	if _grid.is_empty():
		return _height_at(x, z)
	var fx := (x + _grid_half) / _grid_cell
	var fz := (z + _grid_half) / _grid_cell
	fx = clampf(fx, 0.0, float(_grid_n - 1) - 0.001)
	fz = clampf(fz, 0.0, float(_grid_n - 1) - 0.001)
	var ix := int(fx)
	var iz := int(fz)
	var tx := fx - float(ix)
	var tz := fz - float(iz)
	var r0 := iz * _grid_n + ix
	var r1 := r0 + _grid_n
	var h00: float = _grid[r0]
	var h10: float = _grid[r0 + 1]
	var h01: float = _grid[r1]
	var h11: float = _grid[r1 + 1]
	return lerpf(lerpf(h00, h10, tx), lerpf(h01, h11, tx), tz)


func normal_at(x: float, z: float) -> Vector3:
	## 地表法线（中心差分，与 shader 顶点法线同公式），供草/杂物沿坡倾斜
	var e := 0.5
	var h := _height_at(x, z)
	var hx := _height_at(x + e, z)
	var hz := _height_at(x, z + e)
	return Vector3(h - hx, e, h - hz).normalized()


func _height_at(x: float, z: float) -> float:
	var n := _fbm(Vector2(x, z) * frequency)
	var n2 := _fbm(Vector2(x, z) * frequency * 4.0 + Vector2(17.0, 3.0))
	var n3 := _fbm(Vector2(x, z) * frequency * 6.0 + Vector2(7.0, 11.0))
	return (n * 0.75 + n2 * 0.25 + n3 * 0.12) * height_amp * 2.0 - height_amp


func _build_terrain_mesh() -> void:
	# 注意：大 ArrayMesh 在本机环境渲染有 bug（顶点数多时整个 mesh 不可见），
	# 地面改用 PlaneMesh（PrimitiveMesh 渲染正常）+ shader 顶点位移生成起伏。
	var plane := PlaneMesh.new()
	plane.size = Vector2(size, size)
	plane.subdivide_width = segments
	plane.subdivide_depth = segments

	var mat := ShaderMaterial.new()
	mat.shader = GROUND_SHADER
	mat.set_shader_parameter("height_amp", height_amp)
	mat.set_shader_parameter("frequency", frequency)
	mat.set_shader_parameter("height_step", size / float(segments))
	mat.set_shader_parameter("albedo_tex", load("res://assets/ground/leafy_grass_diff_2k.jpg"))
	mat.set_shader_parameter("normal_tex", load("res://assets/ground/leafy_grass_nor_gl_2k.jpg"))
	mat.set_shader_parameter("rough_tex", load("res://assets/ground/leafy_grass_rough_2k.jpg"))
	plane.material = mat

	var mi := MeshInstance3D.new()
	mi.mesh = plane
	add_child(mi)


func _build_collision() -> void:
	## 地形碰撞：三角网格（ConcavePolygonShape3D）采样同一高度场。
	## 起伏变大后 Box 网格近似会形成台阶卡住玩家，trimesh 在物理帧后创建已验证稳定。
	var shape := ConcavePolygonShape3D.new()
	shape.set_faces(_build_collision_faces())
	var body := StaticBody3D.new()
	var csc := CollisionShape3D.new()
	csc.shape = shape
	body.add_child(csc)
	add_child(body)


func _build_collision_faces() -> PackedVector3Array:
	## 按网格分辨率采样地形，展开为三角形汤（与视觉 mesh 同密度）。
	## 先缓存 (segments+1)^2 个顶点高度再连三角形：直接逐顶点调用 _height_at
	## 会有 6 倍冗余（每格 6 顶点但仅 4 个唯一角点），启动耗时大头即在此。
	var n := segments + 1
	var half := size * 0.5
```

```json
shader_type spatial;

uniform vec3 color_a : source_color = vec3(0.30, 0.54, 0.22);
uniform vec3 color_b : source_color = vec3(0.44, 0.69, 0.32);
uniform vec3 color_dry : source_color = vec3(0.62, 0.56, 0.28);
uniform vec3 color_soil : source_color = vec3(0.38, 0.30, 0.19);
uniform float patch_scale = 0.10;
uniform float detail_scale = 5.0;
uniform float repeat = 40.0;

// 照片级草地纹理（Poly Haven leafy_grass，CC0）
uniform sampler2D albedo_tex : source_color, filter_linear_mipmap, repeat_enable;
uniform sampler2D normal_tex : filter_linear_mipmap, repeat_enable;
uniform sampler2D rough_tex : filter_linear_mipmap, repeat_enable;
uniform float tex_repeat = 60.0;

// 地形起伏参数（与 terrain.gd 的 height_at 完全一致，保证草/碰撞对齐）
uniform float height_amp : hint_range(0.0, 15.0) = 13.0;
uniform float frequency = 0.009;
uniform float height_step = 3.125;

varying float v_world_y;
varying vec2 v_world_xz;

float hash21(vec2 p) {
	p = fract(p * vec2(123.34, 456.21));
	p += dot(p, p + 45.32);
	return fract(p.x * p.y);
}

float vnoise(vec2 p) {
	vec2 i = floor(p);
	vec2 f = fract(p);
	f = f * f * (3.0 - 2.0 * f);
	float a = hash21(i);
	float b = hash21(i + vec2(1.0, 0.0));
	float c = hash21(i + vec2(0.0, 1.0));
	float d = hash21(i + vec2(1.0, 1.0));
	return mix(mix(a, b, f.x), mix(c, d, f.x), f.y);
}

float fbm(vec2 p) {
	float v = 0.0;
	float amp = 0.5;
	for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
		v += amp * vnoise(p);
		p = vec2(p.x * 0.8 + p.y * 0.6, -0.6 * p.x + 0.8 * p.y) * 2.02;
		amp *= 0.5;
	}
	return v;
}

// 轻量 3 倍频版本：用于 fragment 里的大尺度色斑/云影（视觉几乎无差，省 ~40% 噪声计算）
float fbm3(vec2 p) {
	float v = 0.0;
	float amp = 0.5;
	for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
		v += amp * vnoise(p);
		p = vec2(p.x * 0.8 + p.y * 0.6, -0.6 * p.x + 0.8 * p.y) * 2.02;
		amp *= 0.5;
	}
	return v;
}

float terrain_height(vec2 p) {
	float n = fbm(p * frequency);
	float n2 = fbm(p * frequency * 4.0 + vec2(17.0, 3.0));
	float n3 = fbm(p * frequency * 6.0 + vec2(7.0, 11.0));
	return (n * 0.75 + n2 * 0.25 + n3 * 0.12) * height_amp * 2.0 - height_amp;
}

void vertex() {
	// 顶点位移生成起伏地形（与 CPU 端 height_at 同公式），并重算法线
	vec2 p = VERTEX.xz;
	float h = terrain_height(p);
	float hx = terrain_height(p + vec2(height_step, 0.0));
	float hz = terrain_height(p + vec2(0.0, height_step));
	NORMAL = normalize(vec3(h - hx, height_step, h - hz));
	VERTEX.y += h;
	v_world_y = VERTEX.y;
```

#### Thinking

Important discovery regarding ground clarity:

1. The texture's `.import` has `mipmaps/generate=false` — but the shader is using `filter_linear_mipmap` sampling! Sampling a texture without mipmaps using linear_mipmap results in blurry/noisy appearance or fallback. In fact, in Godot, if you load a texture without mipmaps and sample it with a mipmap filter, it becomes blurry or aliasing occurs. For a ground that repeats 60 times, this is the main cause of blur.

2. `compress/mode=0` = lossless VRAM compression? In Godot 4, mode 0 = Lossless. Actually, mode 0 is lossless. No problem there.

3. `tex_repeat = 60.0` across 500m means each tile covers about 8.3m. A 2K texture over 8.3m is about 245 texels/m — that's sufficient. The cause of blurriness is probably: (a) lack of mipmaps, (b) no anisotropic filtering.

Ground clarity fix:
- Set `mipmaps/generate=true` on the 3 ground textures (diffuse, normal, roughness).
- Add anisotropic filtering: In the shader, `filter_anisotropic` is needed — Godot's spatial shader texture hints: `filter_linear_mipmap_anisotropic`. Change the uniform hint to `filter_linear_mipmap_anisotropic`.
- Also, confirm that the project's max anisotropy is high (default is 4x? Actually, the default of `rendering/textures/default_filters/anisotropic_filtering_level` is 2, meaning 4x).

Let's check the fragment part of the shader to see how the textures are sampled (texture() uses the filter set by the hint). And also check the project settings for anisotropy.

But the biggest problem is that mipmaps/generate=false. Let's set it to true on all 3 ground textures and re-import.

```json
==== shader fragment (texture sampling) ====
	v_world_y = VERTEX.y;
	v_world_xz = VERTEX.xz;
}

void fragment() {
	vec2 uv = UV * tex_repeat;
	vec3 albedo = texture(albedo_tex, uv).rgb;
	// 叠加少量程序化色斑，丰富大尺度明暗；轻微绿色增益让地面与草协调
	float patch = fbm3(uv * patch_scale * 3.0);
	float dry = fbm3(uv * patch_scale * 5.0 + 3.1);
	albedo *= (0.90 + 0.18 * patch) * vec3(0.92, 1.12, 0.90);
	albedo = mix(albedo, color_dry, smoothstep(0.72, 0.92, dry) * 0.25);

	// 按海拔着色：低谷更深绿、山脊偏干黄，让地形起伏一眼可辨
	float h01 = clamp((v_world_y + height_amp) / max(height_amp * 2.0, 0.001), 0.0, 1.0);
	albedo *= mix(vec3(0.80, 1.22, 0.72), vec3(1.32, 0.94, 0.64), h01);

	// 云朵阴影：世界坐标锚定的云层缓慢飘移，云下地面变暗
	float cloud = fbm3(v_world_xz * 0.012 + vec2(TIME * 0.04, TIME * 0.028));
	float cloud_shadow = mix(1.0, 0.70, smoothstep(0.52, 0.85, cloud));
	albedo *= cloud_shadow;

	ALBEDO = albedo;
	ROUGHNESS = texture(rough_tex, uv).r;
	// 法线贴图（GL 约定，手动解包）
	vec3 n = texture(normal_tex, uv).rgb * 2.0 - 1.0;
	NORMAL_MAP = n;
}
```

#### Thinking

Investigation results:
- The shader samples textures with `texture()`, and the hint is `filter_linear_mipmap` — mipmaps are disabled at import time. Fix: enable mipmaps + anisotropic hint (`filter_linear_mipmap_anisotropic`) on the 3 textures and reimport. Also `uv = UV * tex_repeat` — UV of PlaneMesh goes 0..1 over 500m, tex_repeat=60 → 1 tile per 8.3m. 2K texture → 245 texels/m. No problem.
- godotengine.org/asset-library is reachable (200)! The real asset library REST endpoint: does https://godotengine.org/asset-library/api/asset? import re, urllib.request, html as H
```bash
def fetch(url):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={'User-Agent':'Mozilla/5.0'})
    return urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=15).read().decode('utf-8','ignore')
for aid in ['5344','5285','5186','4155']:
    try:
        page = fetch(f'https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/{aid}')
        title = re.search(r'<h1>(.*?)</h1>', page, re.S)
        ver = re.findall(r'Godot (\d\.[\d.x]+)', page)
        dl = re.findall(r'(https://[^\s"<>]+\.(?:zip|tar\.gz))', page)
        desc = re.search(r'class="asset-description"[^>]*>(.*?)</div>', page, re.S)
        d = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>|\s+',' ', desc.group(1))[:200] if desc else ''
        print(f'--- {aid} {H.unescape(title.group(1)).strip() if title else "?"}')
        print('   godot:', sorted(set(ver))[:4])
        for u in dl[:3]: print('   dl:', H.unescape(u))
        print('   ', H.unescape(d).strip()[:180])
    except Exception as e:
        print(aid, 'ERR', e)
EOF
```

```json
==== grid-inventory scripts ====
@tool
extends Panel
class_name InventorySlot
## One visual slot. Handles drag and drop; rendering is driven by refresh().

var inventory: Inventory
var index: int = 0

@onready var _icon: TextureRect = $Icon
@onready var _placeholder: ColorRect = $Placeholder


func setup(inv: Inventory, slot_index: int) -> void:
	inventory = inv
	index = slot_index
	refresh()


func refresh() -> void:
	var slot = inventory.slots[index] if inventory != null else null
	if slot == null:
		_icon.texture = null
		_icon.visible = false
		_placeholder.visible = false
		tooltip_text = ""
		return

	var item: InvItem = slot.item
	if item.icon != null:
		_icon.texture = item.icon
		_icon.visible = true
		_placeholder.visible = false
	else:
		_icon.visible = false
		_placeholder.color = item.color
		_placeholder.visible = true
	tooltip_text = item.name


func _get_drag_data(_pos: Vector2) -> Variant:
	if inventory == null or inventory.slots[index] == null:
		return null
	var src = inventory.slots[index]
	var cr := ColorRect.new()
	cr.color = src.item.color
	cr.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(48, 48)
	set_drag_preview(cr)
	return {"from_index": index}


func _can_drop_data(_pos: Vector2, data: Variant) -> bool:
	return data is Dictionary and data.has("from_index")


func _drop_data(_pos: Vector2, data: Variant) -> void:
	inventory.move_slot(data["from_index"], index)
```
