==== inventory.gd ====
@tool
extends Resource
class_name Inventory
## A fixed-size, slot-based inventory. UI-agnostic — pair it with InventoryUI or
## drive your own interface from the `inventory_changed` signal.
##
## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Grid Inventory LITE: one item per slot, move & swap via drag and drop.
## Grid Inventory PRO adds: stacking & auto-merge with per-item max_stack,
## quantity counters, item tooltips, count_of()/has_item() query helpers, and
## one-call save/load. Same classes, drop-in upgrade:
##   https://godot-forge.itch.io/grid-inventory-godot
## ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

signal inventory_changed
signal item_added(item: InvItem)
signal full(item: InvItem)

@export var size: int = 20:
	set(value):
		size = max(1, value)
		_resize_slots()

## Each slot is either null or {"item": InvItem}.
var slots: Array = []


func _init(slot_count: int = 20) -> void:
	size = slot_count


func _resize_slots() -> void:
	slots.resize(size)


## Places `item` in the first empty slot. Returns true if it fit.
func add_item(item: InvItem) -> bool:
	if item == null:
		return false
	var idx := _first_empty()
	if idx == -1:
		full.emit(item)
		return false
	slots[idx] = {"item": item}
	item_added.emit(item)
	inventory_changed.emit()
	return true


## Removes whatever is in `index`.
func remove_at(index: int) -> void:
	if index < 0 or index >= slots.size():
		return
	if slots[index] != null:
		slots[index] = null
		inventory_changed.emit()


## Swaps the contents of two slots (used by drag and drop).
func move_slot(from_index: int, to_index: int) -> void:
	if from_index == to_index:
		return
	if from_index < 0 or to_index < 0 or from_index >= slots.size() or to_index >= slots.size():
		return
	if slots[from_index] == null:
		return
	var tmp = slots[to_index]
	slots[to_index] = slots[from_index]
	slots[from_index] = tmp
	inventory_changed.emit()


func clear() -> void:
	for i in slots.size():
		slots[i] = null
	inventory_changed.emit()


func _first_empty() -> int:
	for i in slots.size():
		if slots[i] == null:
			return i
	return -1
==== inventory_ui.gd ====
@tool
extends Control
class_name InventoryUI
## Drop this node into your UI, assign an Inventory, and it renders a clickable,
## drag-and-drop grid that stays in sync via the inventory's signal.

const SLOT_SCENE := preload("res://addons/grid_inventory/inventory_slot.tscn")

@export var columns: int = 5:
	set(value):
		columns = max(1, value)
		if _grid != null:
			_grid.columns = columns

## Assign an Inventory resource here (or via set_inventory at runtime).
@export var inventory: Inventory:
	get:
		return _inventory
	set(value):
		set_inventory(value)

var _inventory: Inventory
var _grid: GridContainer
var _slots: Array[InventorySlot] = []


func _ready() -> void:
	if _grid == null:
		_grid = GridContainer.new()
		_grid.columns = columns
		_grid.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_TOP_LEFT)
		add_child(_grid)
	if _inventory != null:
		_rebuild()


func set_inventory(inv: Inventory) -> void:
	if _inventory == inv:
		return
	if _inventory != null and _inventory.inventory_changed.is_connected(_on_changed):
		_inventory.inventory_changed.disconnect(_on_changed)
	_inventory = inv
	if _inventory != null:
		_inventory.inventory_changed.connect(_on_changed)
	if is_inside_tree():
		_rebuild()


func _rebuild() -> void:
	if _grid == null:
		return
	for child in _grid.get_children():
		child.queue_free()
	_slots.clear()
	if _inventory == null:
		return
	for i in _inventory.size:
		var slot: InventorySlot = SLOT_SCENE.instantiate()
		_grid.add_child(slot)
		slot.setup(_inventory, i)
==== LICENSE ====
MIT License

Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy

No, if the texture has no mipmaps and the sampler requests mipmap filtering, it uses LOD 0 (base) with linear → aliasing when minifying (shimmering), and blurry when… hmm. The real sharpness improvement: enable mipmaps (proper LOD, reduces shimmer) + anisotropic filtering (sharp at grazing angles, which is exactly what ground is). Ground viewed at an angle benefits enormously from anisotropic filtering. So: anisotropic + mipmaps.

Implementation:
```
func try_move(src, dst) -> bool:
  var sid = get_item(src), did = get_item(dst)
  # type check for equipment destinations
  if dst is equipment and sid != "" and DB[sid].type != dst.kind: return false
  if src is equipment and did != "" and DB[did].type != src.kind: return false
  set_item(dst, sid); set_item(src, did)
  sync_player(); refresh_all(); return true
```

Alright. So let's implement everything. Edit plan:

**1. dogmilk item icon**: Copy `assets/props/dogmilk/front.png` → `assets/items/dogmilk.png` (the front face of the carton, 301×559 RGBA — a clean 2D image).

**2. Chest icon for dropped item boxes**: Download skoll/open-chest.svg from game-icons, strip the background → assets/items/chest.svg.

**3. game_inventory.gd** — major update:
- Add "dogmilk" to DB: name Wild Dog Milk, slot -1 (usable), icon dogmilk.png, tint white, desc "Use: 10 seconds of invincibility, after duration ends fully restores HP (consumed on use)".
- Auto-equip armor on start: _eq.armor="armor" (don't put it in the bag).
- Selection + double-click use: In SlotCtl's gui_input: track click count/time; single click → inv.select_slot(self); double click → inv.use_slot(self).
- use_slot: dogmilk → consume + player.start_invincibility(10.0); equipment → equip to its slot (swap with current equipment).
- E key while UI is open: drop the selected item → spawn a box in the world.
- add_item(id) API for rewards (returns false if bag is full).
- Box panel UI: show_box(box) displays items; click item → take into bag; take all button; close button.
- Difficulty selection panel: show_difficulty_picker() → 3 buttons → callback to player.

**4. player.gd**:
- Invincibility: _inv_t, start_invincibility(t), is_invincible(); take_damage early-returns while invincible; tick in _physics_process; on expiry → heal to full.
- E routing: _try_interact_boss → if box is nearby (group "drop_box" within 3.5m) → open box; elif near boss → if boss.defeated_count>0 → show difficulty selection, then enter; else enter directly.
- _on_boss_died: grant reward dogmilk × boss.reward_count; schedule boss respawn (boss.revive_after()).
- Weapon guard: set_equipment already handles this; sword/bow check active ✓ (no unequipped → can't trigger is satisfied).

**5. boss.gd**:
- Difficulty system: defeated_count, difficulty, DIFF_HP/DIFF_DMG/DIFF_REWARD arrays; set_difficulty(d) applies max_hp scaling + aura multiplier; _die: defeated_count+=1; revive(delay): reset _dead, hp=max, rise back up, go_home.
- AURA_DMG scaling in _update_windup: player.take_damage(AURA_DMG * DIFF_DMG[difficulty]).
- Reward count getter.
- set_arena_mode(true) applies difficulty HP.

**6. hud.gd**: Invincibility display — while player.is_invincible(): _bar.modulate to gold + label "Invincible"; on expiry → white. "HP bar shows permanently" → HP bar stays visible (it's always visible anyway) — interpret as persistent gold "Invincible" display.

**7. drop_box.gd** — small script for box Node3D: Sprite3D chest icon + Label3D; holds items array; group "drop_box".

Spawn position: player's global_position + facing direction × 1.5. In arena, box is on arena floor; in overworld, on ground. Box y: player's y - 1 (feet) + 0.5.

Box opening flow: player presses E near box → inventory.show_box(box): overlay panel lists box items as SlotCtl (bag-style) — click item → move to player's bag (if full → stays in box, show hint). Buttons: Take All, Close (Tab/Esc/E). Box items stored in box.items (Array[String]).

Difficulty selection flow: player near boss (defeated_count>=1) presses E → inventory.show_difficulty(): panel with 3 buttons: Easy (HP 1000/Damage 1.0x/Reward 2), Normal (1500/1.5x/3), Hard (2000/2x/4). Click → player._enter_arena_with_difficulty(d).

Note: E key while inventory is open = drop selected item. But difficulty/box panels also use E? Box panel: E/Tab to close. Drop: only when inventory panel is open AND a slot with an item is selected. To avoid conflicts: if box panel is open → E closes it; if inventory is open → E drops.

Respawn: after _die, sink animation runs in _process (visual y decreases). Respawn: after 5 seconds: reset visual y to 0.12, _dead=false, hp=max_hp (base), label text back to original, go_home. Player is already outside the arena (auto-exit at 3 seconds). Boss's arena_mode is set to false by _exit_arena.

Reward: player._on_boss_died → inv.add_item("dogmilk") × boss.reward_count() (2/3/4). If bag is full → skip? Just try adding, ignore failures (or drop a box? Keep it simple: ignore).

Auto-equip armor on start: _eq.armor = "armor". So the armor slot shows armor from the beginning, and player's armor_factor=0.5 from the start! Hmm — this makes the game easier from the beginning. The user said "auto-equip armor" — yes, they want it equipped. OK.

func _ready() -> void:
	add_to_group("boss")
	var ground := get_node_or_null("../Ground")
	if ground != null and ground.has_method("height_at"):
		_base_y = ground.height_at(world_x, world_z)
	position = Vector3(world_x, _base_y, world_z)
	_home_pos = position

	_visual = Node3D.new()
	add_child(_visual)
	var mi := MeshInstance3D.new()
	mi.mesh = _build_box_mesh()
	mi.scale = Vector3.ONE * scale_factor
	_visual.add_child(mi)

	# 实体碰撞（剑射线与玩家阻挡）
	var body := StaticBody3D.new()
	body.add_to_group("boss")
	var csc := CollisionShape3D.new()
	var box := BoxShape3D.new()
	box.size = Vector3(0.09, 0.25, 0.06) * scale_factor
	csc.shape = box
==== player _on_boss_died + _ready ====
	hp = max_hp
	_spawn_pos = _find_spawn()
	global_position = _spawn_pos
	_sword = get_node_or_null("Camera3D/Sword")
	if _sword != null:
		_sword.connect("slash_hit", _on_slash_hit)
	_bow = get_node_or_null("Camera3D/Bow")
	if _bow != null:
		_bow.set_active(false)
	_boss = get_node_or_null("../Boss")
	if _boss != null:
		_boss.connect("died", _on_boss_died)
	_arena = get_node_or_null("../Arena")


func _on_boss_died() -> void:
	## BOSS 在空间中被击败：等沉地动画播完后自动送回大地图
	if not _in_arena:
		return
	get_tree().create_timer(3.0).timeout.connect(_exit_arena)
